claims.claim: A coding agent such as Claude Code can write a PromptArena kit: prompts, scenarios, assertions, tools and mock responses.
PromptArena ships the config format and idioms inside the binary and writes them into the project as an authoring brief.
promptarena init my-kit --quick
init accepts --quick
init scaffolds a sample kit and writes the brief next to it
init accepts --template <name>
promptarena examples list lists the template catalog
init accepts --no-agent, which skips writing the brief
promptarena agent-brief writes the brief into the current directory by default
promptarena agent-brief ./my-kit accepts a target directory argument
agent-brief writes only the brief, with no sample kit
The brief writes AGENTS.md, a short pointer to the skill, workflow and common mistakes
The brief writes .claude/skills/promptarena-authoring/SKILL.md with a step-by-step workflow and minimal valid skeletons per config kind
The skill reference directory holds evals-and-assertions.md, config-fields.md, mock-responses.md and cli.md, generated from the binary
If AGENTS.md already exists, the brief is appended once and the user's content is kept
The skill and reference files are overwritten on each agent-brief run
promptarena mcp runs a stdio MCP server
The MCP server exposes four tools: explain, get_schema, list_examples, show_example
.mcp.json is the project file Claude Code reads for MCP servers
The .mcp.json example uses mcpServers.promptarena with command "promptarena" and args ["mcp"]
Any MCP client can run the same promptarena mcp command
Claude Code loads .claude/skills/ and AGENTS.md from the project
Codex and other agents that read AGENTS.md pick up the brief from it
The skill tells the agent to settle measurable success criteria before writing any prompts
Each success-criteria answer becomes an assertion or eval, and those are the spec
The agent asks for identity, tone and guidelines rather than inventing them
The agent asks for an MCP server, an API or OpenAPI spec, or sample payloads when tool data lives in a backend
In a non-interactive run (claude -p, CI) the agent writes mode: mock tools and lists invented contracts as assumptions
mode: mock
promptarena validate config.arena.yaml
promptarena run --ci --formats json,markdown
run accepts --ci
run accepts --formats with values json and markdown
validate checks each file against the JSON schema embedded in the binary
validate checks that every assertion type exists
validate builds the pack in memory and runs every check packc runs
A config that passes validate compiles with packc
validate reports every problem in one pass rather than stopping at the first
validate --json gives the same report as JSON
Each validate problem names the stage that found it and the file to edit
run --ci runs every scenario headless
run --ci writes results to the out/ directory
out/results.md holds the summary and per-run JSON files hold detail
Mock responses in mock-responses.yaml are keyed by each scenario's metadata.name
Tools, workflow state and memory run for real against mocked model output
Self-play personas include cooperative, confused, impatient and adversarial
A provider with type: mock is a valid provider config
run accepts --mock-provider
--mock-provider replaces every provider with a generic mock that ignores canned responses
A kind: Tool config is a contract with name, description, input_schema and output_schema plus a binding
Tool mode mock is a valid tool mode
Tool mode live takes an http block
Tool mode mcp is a valid tool mode
Tool mode exec runs only in the PromptKit SDK, not in promptarena run
Tool implementations live outside the pack
promptarena run opens an interactive terminal UI when run in a terminal
The interactive TUI cannot run inside an agent session
promptarena serve starts the web UI
serve accepts --open to launch a browser
The agent can start promptarena serve as a background task
promptarena chat lets the user talk to the agent under test
promptarena deploy ships the kit
The agent can write a CI workflow that validates, runs and deploys the kit
